title: Reference genomes and fossils revise bat family phylogeny and biogeography.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Dryad API metadata for doi:10.5061/dryad.1rn8pk187: 21 files, total storage 1,485,971,138,931 bytes (~1.49 TB). Largest are Section_6.tgz (278.7 GB), Section_8 Cactus HAL alignment (268.8 GB) and six MAF (multiple alignment format) whole-genome alignments of 66-257 GB each; small files are Assemblies_and_species.tsv (<0.1 MB), Section_14/18 (0.5 MB), Section_7 (1.3 MB), Section_15 (6 MB). Direct file downloads via the Dryad v2 API returned HTTP 401 (unauthorised), so no file contents were opened. GitHub repo Bat1K-21families/21families-analyses holds only a README pointing to other code repositories; no data tables.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: 103 bat species genomes (42 new), all 21 families; morphological matrix of 699 characters for 65 species including 44 fossils; 26 ancestral chromosomes; genome accessions in Supplementary Table 1.1 (supplement listing timed out, not retrieved).

a1_downloadable.note: Dryad record is public and file listing is open; programmatic download via the v2 API returned 401, but browser download is presumably open (not verified). Not the deciding failure.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: The paper's outputs are phylogenetic trees, divergence dates, ancestral karyotypes and biogeographic reconstructions; there is no measured per-item outcome column to predict. Any label (e.g. per-window gene-tree topology) would have to be constructed by running tree inference. Judged from file listing and paper text, not file contents.

a3_inputs_present.note: Genome alignments and assemblies are deposited (listing seen), but only as 66-279 GB files.

a4_units_stated.note: Not applicable in a meaningful way; no label table exists to check.

a5_enough_rows.note: The natural unit is the species: 103 genomes and 65 taxa in the morphological matrix (paper text). Far below ~400 even for classification; row counts not verified in files.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~1.49 TB total on Dryad; alignments 66-279 GB each
a6_fits_laptop.note: Any genome-scale feature set needs the multi-hundred-GB alignments; the small files are summaries for ~100 species.

a8_label_provenance.note: Candidate labels (window topologies, divergence times, ancestral states, ancestral ranges) are all outputs of phylogenetic models, not physical measurements.

honest_claim_h3: No ML claim is supportable: the dataset is ~100 species and trees inferred from them, with no measured per-item outcome.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use per-species bat genome features to predict traits such as echolocation type or hibernation across the bat family tree.
plain_idea.train_on: One row per bat species (103 genomes, from paper text), with genome-wide features summarised from the deposited alignments.
plain_idea.predict: A species-level trait taken from the literature, or a per-genome-window tree topology inferred by phylogenetic software; neither is a measured column in this deposit.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Would link genome content to bat adaptations, but with ~100 related species it is a comparative-genomics problem, not an ML one.

ml_idea: None viable. Species-level trait prediction has n≈103 phylogenetically non-independent rows; per-window topology classification uses labels produced by tree-inference software from the same alignments (circular), and needs 66-279 GB alignment files.

effort.compute_note: Sizes taken from Dryad file metadata; nothing timed.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count of labelled units: 103 species (paper) — already fails A5.

verdict_reason: Phylogenomics resource with no measured label column (A2), only ~103 species as units (A5), labels that are tree-inference outputs (A8), and a ~1.49 TB deposit whose genome-scale files are 66-279 GB each (A6).
